FRENCH ULTRAMARINE VALUE STUDY
case · 5 tones · values 3.1 to 8.1 · Winsor & Newton Artisan · 5 tones

PAINTS
- Winsor & Newton Artisan French Ultramarine (PB29): Your main color. The light and middle tones are this plus white.
- Winsor & Newton Artisan Titanium White: Opaque, strong white. The light tones are mostly white, so have plenty.
- Water-mixable linseed oil or medium: Optional. A drop loosens stiff mixes. Clean brushes with water.

TONES (darkest to lightest)
Tone 1 | value 3.1 | 10% of image | 2.5 parts French Ultramarine : 1 part white (69% French Ultramarine by volume)
Tone 2 | value 4.3 | 22% of image | 1 part French Ultramarine : 2 parts white (35% French Ultramarine by volume)
Tone 3 | value 5.2 | 34% of image | 1 part French Ultramarine : 4 parts white (19% French Ultramarine by volume)
Tone 4 | value 5.9 | 23% of image | 1 part French Ultramarine : 7 parts white (12% French Ultramarine by volume)
Tone 5 | value 8.1 | 11% of image | 1 part French Ultramarine : 55 parts white (2% French Ultramarine by volume)

TIPS
1. Mix every tone before you start painting, in separate puddles, lightest to darkest. Make more of the tones with the largest share of the image.
2. For the light tones, add the ultramarine into the white a little at a time. French Ultramarine is far stronger than white, so going the other way wastes paint.
3. For the darkest tones, add the phthalo blue into the ultramarine with the knife tip, a little at a time. Too much shifts the hue.
4. Check each puddle by dabbing it on a scrap card and holding it against the same area of a grayscale print of your photo. Squint to compare.
5. Keep the oil content low in early layers (fat over lean), especially if you will paint color over this study later.
6. Paint in tone order: block in the darkest shapes first, then work up to the lights.

Ratios are model estimates by volume. Test each mix on a card against your reference.

- Winsor & Newton Artisan Yellow Ochre (PY42): The palette's yellow. With black it makes muted olive greens. Used in 5 of 8 mixes.
- Winsor & Newton Artisan Cadmium Red Light (PR108): The palette's red. Warms skin, lips and shadows. Used in 3 of 8 mixes.

- Winsor & Newton Artisan Titanium White: Lightens every mix. Used in 8 of 8 mixes, so have plenty.
- Water-mixable linseed oil or medium: Optional. A drop loosens stiff mixes. Clean brushes with water.

TIPS
1. Mix every color before you start, in separate puddles. Make more of the colors with the largest share of the picture.
2. Match value first, then hue. Dab each mix on a card next to the same area of your photo and squint. A mix with the right value but slightly off hue still reads correctly.
3. Zorn has no real blue. Ivory Black with white looks blue-gray next to the warm ochre and red, so let it do the job of blue in skies, eyes and shadows.
4. For skin, start from Yellow Ochre, Cadmium Red Light and white, then cool the shadow side with a little of the black-and-white gray.
5. Keep the oil content low in early layers (fat over lean).
6. Paint from dark to light: block in the darkest shapes first, then work up to the lights.
